source: PROVISIONAL (milk-24): FAO 2019 (ca5644en.pdf) Table 1 Group 1 definition (p.11): "Edible parts of plants (fruit, seeds, leaves, stems, roots, tubers) or of or from animals (muscle, fat, offal, eggs, milk), and also fungi, algae, all after separation from nature." and example "fresh, powdered or pasteurized milk": milk is placed as an animal food with NO species restriction. Inference level: class-instance of the animal milk named by FAO (same level as goat milk and sheep milk). Identity: FSSAI Chapter 2.1 Dairy products and analogues (full PDF, 81 pages, Version 3 of 07.05.2025, https://www.fssai.gov.in/docs/food-law/regulations/compendium/food-products-standards/Chapter%202_1_Dairy_products_and_analogues.pdf) clause 2.1.2(1)(a) lists "species identified milk ... namely buffalo milk, cow milk, goat milk, sheep milk and camel milk", and the 2.1.2 composition table gives "Camel Milk" (All India, minimum fat 2.0%, SNF 6.0%). No FDC record. Does not cover: standardised or recombined milk, flavoured or sweetened milk, milk fractions, camel milk powder (abstains), or human milk.
